name: Azure Storage Accounts
tagline: The namespace for blobs, files, queues and tables.
whatItIs: A storage account provides a unique namespace and endpoints for Azure Storage data services, with settings for performance, redundancy, networking, encryption and data protection.
primaryPurpose: Durable, highly available, scalable storage for any data type.
keyFeatures: Standard GPv2 and Premium account types
Encryption at rest with Microsoft- or customer-managed keys
security: Prefer Entra ID over shared keys; consider disabling shared key access
Use SAS with least privilege and short expiry
Require secure transfer (HTTPS) and a minimum TLS version
networking: Public endpoint with firewall rules (VNets, IPs, resource instances, trusted services)
Private endpoints per sub-resource (blob, file, queue, table, dfs, web)
pricing: Pay for capacity (by tier and redundancy), operations/transactions, data retrieval for cool/cold/archive, and geo-replication egress.

confusedWith.name: Managed disks
confusedWith.difference: Disks are separate managed resources, not storage accounts you manage.

relevanceNote: Creating and configuring accounts, redundancy, encryption and access are all tested.
examTips: Name: 3–24 lowercase letters and numbers, globally unique

name: Azure Blob Storage
tagline: Massively scalable object storage with hot-to-archive tiers.
whatItIs: Object storage for unstructured data organized in containers, accessed via HTTPS REST APIs and SDKs.
primaryPurpose: Store large amounts of unstructured data cost-effectively.
keyFeatures: Versioning, soft delete, point-in-time restore, immutability
security: Entra ID data roles (Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor/Owner)
networking: Accessed through the storage account's blob endpoint, firewall and private endpoints
pricing: Capacity by tier, operations, and data retrieval/early-deletion fees for cooler tiers.

confusedWith.name: Azure Files
confusedWith.difference: Files provides mountable SMB/NFS shares; Blob is HTTP object storage.

relevanceNote: Containers, tiers, lifecycle, versioning and soft delete are explicit skills.
examTips: Archive is offline — rehydrate before reading
Lifecycle rules run about once a day

name: Azure Files
tagline: Fully managed SMB and NFS file shares.
whatItIs: Cloud file shares mountable from Windows, Linux and macOS, with identity-based access and snapshot protection.
primaryPurpose: Replace or extend file servers and provide shared storage for apps.
useCases: Hybrid caching with Azure File Sync
keyFeatures: Identity-based auth (AD DS, Entra Domain Services, Entra Kerberos)
security: Share-level RBAC roles plus NTFS ACLs
Private endpoints to keep traffic private
networking: SMB uses TCP 445 — often blocked by ISPs; use VPN/ExpressRoute or File Sync
pricing: Provisioned (premium) or pay-as-you-go/provisioned v2 by capacity and transactions depending on tier and billing model.

confusedWith.name: Azure NetApp Files
confusedWith.difference: Enterprise NAS service for high-performance workloads; Azure Files is the general-purpose managed share.

relevanceNote: Creating shares, snapshots, soft delete and identity-based access are in the outline.
examTips: Port 445 blocked → can't mount over internet
Snapshot = restore files; soft delete = restore deleted share

name: Azure File Sync
tagline: Cache Azure file shares on Windows Servers.
whatItIs: A service that synchronizes Azure file shares with Windows Servers, optionally tiering cold files to the cloud.
primaryPurpose: Hybrid file services: local performance with central cloud storage.
useCases: Fast disaster recovery of a file server
keyFeatures: Storage Sync Service, sync groups, cloud and server endpoints
Cloud tiering (free space and date policies)
networking: Agent uses outbound HTTPS 443 — no need to open SMB 445 to Azure
pricing: Per registered server beyond any included servers, plus underlying Azure Files costs.

confusedWith.name: Robocopy / AzCopy
confusedWith.difference: One-time or scripted copies; File Sync is continuous multi-way sync with tiering.

relevanceNote: Commonly appears in Azure Files scenarios.
examTips: One cloud endpoint per sync group
A server registers with only one Storage Sync Service
